sentences.text: Moganopterus is a large pterosaur with a preserved skull length of about 95 cm and a longest preserved neck vertebra measuring 14.5 cm.
Its skull holds the record for the largest size among all toothed pterosaurs.
Based on its skull and neck size, Moganopterus had a wingspan of about 7 meters, making it one of the largest known ctenochasmatid pterosaurs.
A long and narrow parietal crest on the back of the skull sticks out at a 15° angle to the skull's longitudinal axis.
The animal possessed at least sixty-two teeth in its skull.
The fossil of Moganopterus was found at the village of Xiaosanjiazi near Lamadong in Liaoning Province.
Moganopterus was named and described in 2012 by Lü Junchang, Pu Hanyong, Xu Li, Wu Yanhua, and Wei Xuefang.
The genus name Moganopterus honors the legendary sword couple Gan Jiang and Mo Ye because of its blade-like jaws and includes the Greek word for wing.
The holotype specimen was found in the Barremian-aged Yixian Formation approximately 125 million years ago.
The Moganopterus holotype is housed in the Geological Museum of Henan.
Moganopterus possessed very elongated jaws with straight edges.
The fenestra nasoantorbitalis in Moganopterus is a large rectangular opening representing 22% of the snout length.
Excluding the crest, the Moganopterus skull is 11.5 times longer than it is tall.
The neck vertebrae of Moganopterus are five times longer than they are high.
The lower jaws of Moganopterus are 68.5 cm long and lack a keel.
Hollow structures reinforced by struts are present in the parietal crest and vertebrae of Moganopterus.
In 2012, Moganopterus was classified within the family Boreopteridae and subfamily Moganopterinae.
Moganopterus is placed within the superfamily Ornithocheiroidea.
Moganopterus lived during the Early Cretaceous in western Liaoning Province, China.
Moganopterus lived from the Barremian to the Aptian, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
Some researchers, such as Longrich, Martill, and Andres (2018), place Moganopterus within the Ctenochasmatidae rather than the Boreopteridae.
